(1) we introduce PointFlowNet, a deep network that predicts 3D rigid motion and scene flow from unorganized 3D point clouds, (2) we propose a translation equivariance layer for CNNs, which allows to infer rigid body motion, and (3) we introduce a large-scale synthetic dataset that realistically models sensor noise and occlusions.
we propose to estimate scene flow from un-structured point clouds using deep learning, and that we propose to use a translation equivariant network to circumvent the problem of rigid body motion.

(i) a global representation of rigid motion prohibits inference by convolutional networks, (ii) a translation equivariant formulation of this representation can be used to train such a model, and (iii) this model achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D scene estimation from point clouds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three aspects: (i) the representation of 3D rigid body motion, (ii) the design of a deep neural network for estimating 3D point flow and (iii) the generation of a large-scale dataset for training.

three main contributions: a) we present the first approach for 3D scene from point clouds, b) we introduce a new translation equivariant representation for rigid body motion, and c) we propose a novel dataset for 3D flow estimation from unstructured point cloud sequences.
